h: לְרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ אֱלוּל, א׳ Rosh Chodesh Elul, 1

p: It is stated in Sefer Yetzirah:
"He made the letter yud king over action, etc.,
and the left hand in the soul,
it is known that the holy Name
has the ten sefiros alluded to in it,
and the letter yud alludes to Chochmah.
And it is stated in Pesach Eliyahu
And perhaps it is to this that
in his commentary on the verse
that the yud was said on account of the thought."

And he said that He made the letter yud king over action,
should be in accordance with wisdom.
actions that are the opposite of good,
"It stands to reason that the right one is for good
and the left one for bad,
'The heart of a wise man is at his right,' etc."
"In her left hand are riches and honor" (Mishlei 3:16):
for those who go to the left with it,
meaning those who have no intention
And similarly they said in Midrash Tanchuma
"The left, which is not extended in mitzvos, etc.;
the right, which is extended in mitzvos,
And this is the intent of Sefer Yetzirah:
which are not the performance of mitzvos,
should nevertheless be with the letter yud,
that is, in accordance with wisdom.
And about this it is said (Koheles 9:10):
to do with your strength, do."
"Your strength" means in accordance with wisdom,
which has the letters of koach mah,
as is written in the Tikkunim
as is written in the holy Zohar
"What have you known, what have you perceived,
what have you searched out," etc.

and they are nefesh, ruach, and neshamah,
corresponding to Asiyah, Beriah, and Yetzirah.
The dwelling place of the nefesh,
"The essence of the blood is the liver";
And the blood is the kelipah of Esav,
of whom they said in the Midrash
שֶׁהוּא שׂוֹנֵא דָּמוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם בְּגוּפוֹ
that he hated the blood of man in his body;
and it corresponds to the kelipah of anger,
And it is the root of all the kelipos,
"At the head of all illnesses am I, blood";
that the liver is the level of Esav.
is there a nefesh of holiness,
for there is the anger of Torah scholars,
which is good from every side,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קפב, ב)
"A young Torah scholar who flares up —
it is the Torah that heats him up."
The dwelling place of the ruach is in the heart,
which is half good and half bad;
and in the heart there are two chambers:
"the heart of a wise man at his right"
and "the heart of a fool at his left";
and it corresponds to the kelipah of desire.
And when he has in this
an intention for the sake of Heaven,
it is from "the heart of a wise man at his right."
The dwelling place of the neshamah is in the brain,
and there it is mostly good;
and it corresponds to the kelipah of honor,
which is the root of the yetzer hara
that was created in the world,
for each one said, "I will reign."
that there should be a nation of Yisrael
who would recognize the power of the Kingship of Heaven,
that He is King of the world;
and it is written of Him (Tehillim 93:1):
"Hashem reigns; He is clothed in grandeur" —
the garment was a kind of grandeur,
and from this pride branched out into creation,
But in truth pride is needed
also for the service of Hashem, blessed be He,
"His heart was lifted up in the ways of Hashem."
that his deeds and his Torah
and each person is obligated to say,
"For my sake the world was created,"
and this is a kind of pride.
And in truth the whole world was created
for the sake of each and every Jew,
שֶׁלֹּא בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹלָמוֹ
for the Holy One, blessed be He, created His world
only so that they should fear Him
one's recognizing the attribute of His Kingship, may His Name be blessed,
"If I am a master, where is My fear?"
וְזֶה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה
And this came about through the receiving of the Torah,
the yoke of His Kingship, may His Name be blessed;
and had a single Jew been missing,
it would have held back the giving of the Torah,
(מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה כִּי תָבוֹא; דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ז, ח)
the Shechinah would not have been revealed upon them,
And this is because there was a precise number
which was so essential for receiving the Torah,
has a portion in the Torah,
a letter or part of a letter,
"There are six hundred thousand letters in the Torah."
is made up of several letters;
וְאִם הָיָה הַתּוֹרָה חֲסֵרָה אוֹת אֶחָד
and if the Torah were missing one letter,
or it was not written properly,
Seemingly this looks like a kind of pride;
but in truth it is needed
for the service of Hashem, blessed be He, as mentioned above,
to push away the enticement of the yetzer hara
that all his service counts for nothing,
which comes from the kelipah of the sadness of the spleen.
But sometimes, from the heart of the fool,
and bring in an invalid pride, Heaven forbid.
of the tefillin of the head,
which corresponds to the crown of "we will hear,"
that is, that words of Torah should enter the heart,
for out of it are the issues of life."
And through words of Torah entering,
he will be saved from invalid pride,
אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁמֵּשִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ
only in one who regards himself as if he does not exist
and words of Torah are likened to water:
מָה מַיִם מַנִּיחִין מָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ וְכוּלֵּי
"Just as water leaves a high place, etc.,
only in one whose mind is humble"
But this does not mean one
whose heart is empty of words of Torah,
who has nothing to be proud about,
as we heard from our holy Rebbe of Izhbitza,
may the memory of the tzaddik be a blessing,
is one whose humility is painted on;
is one who is empty like a wilderness,
so that he has nothing to be proud about.
רַק מִי שֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת מָלֵא תוֹרָה
Rather, it means one who is truly full of Torah,
that everything is from Hashem, blessed be He,
Who graciously granted him Torah out of His love,
as we say in the evening prayer:
"With an everlasting love, the House of Yisrael Your people,
You have loved; Torah and mitzvos, etc.,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and as Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, said,
And about this it is said (Iyov 28:12):
"And wisdom is found from ayin, from nothingness."
And this is the tefillin of the head,
the aspect of the crown of "we will hear."
And the tefillin of the hand
are on the weaker hand, the left hand
which are not the performance of mitzvos,
גַּם כֵּן יִהְיוּ מְקוּשָּׁרִין בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
should also be bound to Hashem, blessed be He.
And it is placed opposite the heart,
to subjugate the desires and thoughts of our heart
to His service, may His Name be blessed.
in both of which is mentioned
(אוֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן מו, סְעִיף קָטָן ב)
that they are unique to Yisrael;
That is, concerning covering the head,
כִּי הֵיכָא דְּתֶהֱוֵי עֲלָךְ אֵימְתָא דִּשְׁמַיָּא
so that the fear of Heaven may be upon you";
'The secret of Hashem is for those who fear Him,'"
in which Torah scholars customarily wrap themselves,
as Rashi, of blessed memory, explains
And when he has an intention
for the sake of Heaven in this,
הוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּבְחִינַת עֲטָרָה עַל הָרֹאשׁ
it too is in the aspect of a crown upon the head,
he said, "The Shechinah is above my head."
And likewise "Who girds Yisrael with might"
"The belt atones for the thoughts of the heart,
over the place where it lies";
for the belt was at the level of their elbows,
"They shall not gird themselves where one sweats"
'And kings shall be your nursing fathers.'"
שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַגְבִּיר עַל הַלֵּב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ
that he be able to prevail over the heart of the fool at his left,
And a Jew needs a belt
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לִבּוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה
so that his heart should not see his nakedness,
and this is for the sake of Heaven.
All the more so the mitzvah of tefillin,
which are the performance of a mitzvah,
"Who has sanctified us with His commandments":
they are certainly in the aspect of crowns,
and they correspond to the crowns of "we will do and we will hear."
Only, at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
when they put "we will do" before "we will hear,"
"Who revealed to My children this secret
which the ministering angels use?" etc.
That is, with the ministering angels
it is fitting for them to put doing first,
since they have no yetzer hara
and have no power to do anything
but the will of the Creator, may His Name be blessed,
needed "we will hear" to come first,
that words of Torah should enter the heart,
the doing, too, to Hashem, blessed be He.
But in truth, this is how creation was made:
that there should be free choice,
that today should be for doing them
and tomorrow for receiving their reward
for were there no free choice,
there would be no room for reward;
and as they said about the days of Mashiach,
אֵין לִי בָהֶם חֵפֶץ (קֹהֶלֶת יב, א)
I have no desire in them' (Koheles 12:1):
these are the days of Mashiach,
in which there is neither merit nor guilt,"
since there will be no yetzer hara.
But at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
שֶׁרוֹצִים לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ
that they wish to do the will of the Creator, may His Name be blessed,
as the Men of the Great Assembly said:
And this is why they then put
And then, at the Giving of the Torah,

when they heard the utterance "I am,"
words of Torah were implanted in their heart;
and when they heard "You shall not have,"
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their heart.
Therefore they then tied on them

would be bound to Hashem, blessed be He,

"You speak with us and we will hear,"

That is, when holiness enters the heart,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא

that it should enter the brain and the heart,
and then it becomes the aspect of a crown,
וּתְפִילִּין שֶׁל יָד עַל יָד כֵּהָה
And the tefillin of the hand are on the weaker hand,
to bind the deeds of the left hand
to Hashem, blessed be He, as well,
the passages of Shema and Vehayah im shamoa,
which are the acceptance of the yoke of the Kingship of Heaven
and the yoke of Torah and mitzvos,
And likewise through the passages of Kadesh
which concern the Exodus from Egypt,
to believe that Hashem, blessed be He,
is the Master of all forces:
גַּם מַעֲשֵׂה יַד שְׂמֹאל בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
the deeds of the left hand, too, to Hashem, blessed be He.
And similarly it is stated in the Pesikta
one angel tied on him a crown
and one tied on him a zoni,
That is, corresponding to the word "we will do,"
they tied on them a belt,
לִקְשׁוֹר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה גַּם כֵּן בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
to bind the deed, too, to Hashem, blessed be He.

And this is "Whatever your hand finds

"with your strength" means with koach mah,
And as for its saying "your strength,"
it is speaking only to a Jew,
who knows that everything is from Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּי הוּא הַנּוֹתֵן לְךָ כֹּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת חָיִל
for it is He Who gives you strength to make wealth."
The meaning of "with your strength" is
that Hashem, blessed be He, has apportioned to you.

And this is the prelude and preparation

And Rabbi Yehoshua disagrees with him
"'And not with money shall you be redeemed':
Both these and those are the words of the living God:
in Tishrei it arose in thought to be created,
and in Nissan it was actually created,
(תּוֹסָפוֹת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כז, א, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל כְּמַאן)

then, when atonement is granted on Yom Kippur,
the coming of the redeemer will be,
וְעַל זֶה קָדַם לוֹ חוֹדֶשׁ אֱלוּל
And for this the month of Elul precedes it,
to rectify the deeds of the left hand
alluded to in the letter yud of the holy Name.

אִי אֶפְשָׁר לֵילֵךְ כׇּל הַיּוֹם בִּתְפִילִּין

and one who has corrupted his body
